category_title: Students accustomed to strict, non-negotiable disciplinary models
minimal_context: The student is participating in a performance-based dance activity in the classroom.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's start the dance activity. I'm going to play the music now, please follow the routine.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Dances to the music but makes an incorrect step)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's stop the music. You made a mistake there.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It was just one wrong step. Why do you always turn to look at where we the Mexicans are when something goes wrong?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We just need to get the steps right. Let's try again.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: That is what bothers me. You stop the music and look right at us like we are doing so many bad things. I'm not participating if you're going to single us out.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's start the dance activity. I'm going to play the music now, please follow the routine.

STUDENT: (Dances to the music but makes an incorrect step)

TUTOR: Let's stop the music. You made a mistake there.

STUDENT: It was just one wrong step. Why do you always turn to look at where we the Mexicans are when something goes wrong?

TUTOR: We just need to get the steps right. Let's try again.

STUDENT: That is what bothers me. You stop the music and look right at us like we are doing so many bad things. I'm not participating if you're going to single us out.

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When a Mexican student makes a mistake during a performance-based activity (dance).

behavior_patterns.condition: she stopsthe music and begins to say, ‘Oh no no stop it! Oh my eyes hurt so much to see so many bad things. ’And she turns to look at where we the Mexicans are
